title: Process monitoring
subtitle: See running processes, then stop them by PID or name

cards.meaning: A process is a running program; PID is its process ID
cards.notes: Monitoring means see what is running, then stop it if needed

cards.front: top vs ps vs kill vs killall
cards.meaning: top = live screen; ps = snapshot; kill = by PID; killall = by name
cards.notes: Memory hook for the four tools in this topic

cards.meaning: Dynamically updating live task list (CPU, memory, PID, user, command)
cards.notes: Refreshes by itself until you quit. Load averages and memory summary sit at the top; the table is the process list

cards.meaning: Quit top
cards.notes: top = dashboard; q to leave

cards.meaning: Sort process list by CPU
cards.notes: Not in the course snippet, but you will hit it

cards.meaning: Sort process list by memory
cards.notes: Not in the course snippet, but you will hit it

cards.meaning: Kill a PID from inside top (asks for PID and signal)
cards.notes: Not in the course snippet, but you will hit it

cards.meaning: Prints a list of processes once (snapshot, not a live UI)
cards.notes: Frozen photo, not a movie

cards.meaning: Snapshot of all users' processes with user-oriented columns, including daemons
cards.notes: Classic BSD-style combo: a + u + x

cards.meaning: Processes of all users (not only yours)
cards.notes: BSD-style flag

cards.meaning: User-oriented columns (USER, %CPU, %MEM, …)
cards.notes: BSD-style flag

cards.meaning: Include processes with no controlling terminal (daemons)
cards.notes: BSD-style flag — why aux catches background services

cards.front: ps aux columns USER PID %CPU %MEM STAT COMMAND
cards.meaning: Columns you read on a ps aux snapshot; use PID with kill
cards.notes: PID is the number you pass to kill

cards.meaning: Find PIDs by name in a snapshot
cards.notes: Careful: grep matches itself too

cards.meaning: Sends a signal to a process by PID
cards.notes: Need the number from ps or top

cards.meaning: SIGTERM (15) — ask the process to exit cleanly
cards.notes: Default signal is TERM — polite stop

cards.meaning: Default kill signal — "please exit cleanly"
cards.notes: Process can catch it and shut down gracefully

cards.meaning: SIGKILL — force stop; process cannot catch or ignore it
cards.notes: Same as -KILL. Does not run cleanup — temp files and child processes may remain. Use when TERM is ignored

cards.meaning: You cannot kill another user's process unless you are root
cards.notes: Permission rule for kill

cards.meaning: Sends the signal to all processes with that command name
cards.notes: Prefer kill PID when you mean one process

cards.meaning: SIGTERM every process named top
cards.notes: Default signal is still TERM

cards.meaning: SIGKILL every process named top
cards.notes: Force by name

cards.meaning: Same as -9; signal by name instead of number
cards.notes: -KILL equals -9

cards.meaning: Kills every Java process, not one PID — dangerous on a busy box
cards.notes: Every match gets the signal
